# Rice noodles

<section class="hmi-quick-read" id="rice-noodles-quick-read" data-hmi-quick-read aria-labelledby="rice-noodles-quick-read-label"><div class="hmi-quick-read-label" id="rice-noodles-quick-read-label">Quick read</div>

Rice noodles in the HMI library has 174 reported results for lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, monomethylarsonic acid, total mercury, methylmercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, V, Se, AsIII and AsV from 14 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/guo2017-asian-rice-derived-products-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Guo K, Wells S, Han FX, Arslan Z, Sun H, Zhang J · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/guo2017-asian-rice-derived-products-metals">Trace Elements and Heavy Metals in Asian Rice-Derived Food Products</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Water, Air, &amp; <strong>Metals measured:</strong>

Lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid and monomethylarsonic acid and others, in 174 results from 14 sources.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/guo2017-asian-rice-derived-products-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Guo K, Wells S, Han FX, Arslan Z, Sun H, Zhang J · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/guo2017-asian-rice-derived-products-metals">Trace Elements and Heavy Metals in Asian Rice-Derived Food Products</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Water, Air, &amp; </li>
<li>
<strong>Main drivers:</strong>

Form, basis and where the rice noodles was sampled; reporting limits decide how many results are non-detects.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/guo2017-asian-rice-derived-products-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Guo K, Wells S, Han FX, Arslan Z, Sun H, Zhang J · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/guo2017-asian-rice-derived-products-metals">Trace Elements and Heavy Metals in Asian Rice-Derived Food Products</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Water, Air, &amp; Soil Pollution</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/guo2017-asian-rice-derived-products-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety (Hong Kong) · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Metallic Contaminants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

<li>
<strong>Practical framing:</strong>

Ask for lot results with a quantification limit well below the limit that applies in the destination market.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/guo2017-asian-rice-derived-products-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Guo K, Wells S, Han FX, Arslan Z, Sun H, Zhang J · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/guo2017-asian-rice-derived-products-metals">Trace Elements and Heavy Metals in Asian Rice-Derived Food Products</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Water, Air, &amp; For a buyer the practical points are the form bought, the basis a result is reported on, where the rice noodles came from and the laboratory’s reporting limit. Testing finds contamination but does not remove it.

## What counts as rice noodles

<a id="hmi-ing-001"></a>
<a id="what-commodity-biological-species-edible-part-and-commercial-forms-does-this-page-cover"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-002"></a>
<a id="which-processing-states-and-derivatives-are-distinct-materials-rather-than-synonyms"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-003"></a>

<div class="hmi-analyte-explorer" id="hmi-occurrence-rice-noodles" data-analyte-explorer data-compact-intro="true" data-source-summaries="true"><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-explorer-context><summary data-open-context aria-haspopup="dialog" aria-controls="hmi-occurrence-rice-noodles-drawer">Comparison methods and scope</summary><div data-explorer-context-content>

<p>Each row is one statistic a source reports for one form of rice noodles, group and metal; percentiles, ranges and maxima reported for the same samples as a mean or median are shown on that row. Different forms and preparation states are kept apart, and dry-weight results never share a reference with as-sold or fresh-weight results. Ratings place a result against an HMI reference built from monitoring results and ordinary-setting medians for the same form and basis. Same-study contrasts compare a contaminated or treated site with its control, targeted with random sampling, a prepared form with the unprocessed one, or one group of a study with the median of its other groups. Held rows failed a check against their own source and are shown but not compared.</p>

dataset methods and interpretation</summary><div data-shared-evidence-content><p>Source summaries retain their original statistic, material, basis and censoring. Each source drawer identifies methods and overlapping samples. No matched reference or pooled distribution is inferred.</p></div></details><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure" data-baseline-fallback id="hmi-reference-hmi-pooled-reference-v2:rice-noodles-d5307bc0b450:551c004c797e"><summary>HMI rice noodles Pb reference · Rice noodles, as sold</summary><div data-baseline-reference-template="hmi-pooled-reference-v2:rice-noodles-d5307bc0b450:551c004c797e"><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Reference and scope</p><p>HMI rice noodles Pb reference · Rice noodles, as sold. Rice noodles, as sold; As sold, as eaten or fresh weight, µg/kg; no moisture conversion. Distribution of subgroup median concentration values.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Reference (µg/kg)</th><th scope="col">Q1</th><th scope="col">Median</th><th scope="col">Q3</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>Primary HMI reference</td><td>≤3.57</td><td>2.8–14 (bounded)</td><td>9–23.5 (bounded)</td></tr><tr><td>Alternative weighting</td><td>≤4.29</td><td>2.4–14 (bounded)</td><td>9–23.5 (bounded)</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p>15 reference units; 1 sampling family. Counts describe evidence units, not independent studies or certainty.</p><div class="hmi-drawer-table"><table><thead><tr><th scope="col">Contributing family</th><th scope="col">Reference units</th><th scope="col">Weight</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>WHO GEMS/Food</td><td>15</td><td>100%</td></tr></tbody></table></div><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Methods</p><p>HMI pools subgroup medians for rice noodles, as sold on a as sold, as eaten or fresh weight basis: monitoring results summarized as one median per reporting region, sampling type and collection year, total diet composites and printed sample values as single observations, and printed subgroup medians from ordinary farms or markets. Each sampling family has equal total weight. Non-detects stay as zero-to-limit intervals, so quartiles carry lower and upper bounds. Means, ranges and maxima never enter as observations. Other forms, other bases, targeted sampling and results from mining, industrial, wastewater-affected, experimental, fertiliser or manufacturer settings are kept out of this reference.</p><p>Inverse weighted empirical CDF; midpoint at exact cumulative-weight boundaries. At least four reference units and a definitely positive Q1 to Q3 spread are required. This is a display eligibility rule, not statistical validation.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Limitations</p><p>WHO GEMS/Food is the only compatible sampling family for rice noodles, as sold on this basis in the completed rice noodles ledger, so this single-family reference cannot represent other markets. Reporting regions and purchase markets are not growing areas. Non-detects with differing limits widen the bounds. A position is descriptive concentration, not a safety or compliance judgment.</p><p class="hmi-drawer-section-title" role="heading" aria-level="3">Admitted source families</p><ul><li><a href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" class="internal" data-slug="sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020" data-no-cite-meta>FDA Total Diet Study</a></li></ul><details class="hmi-drawer-disclosure"><summary>Reference version and interpretation</summary><p>Frozen evidence selection: 2026-10-22. Targeted rice noodles, as sold samples in EURO had inorganic arsenic higher at 133 µg/kg, against 79 µg/kg for EURO in the same study.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>



<a id="processing-effects-and-derivatives"></a>
## Processing, cooking and preparation

<a id="hmi-ing-016"></a>
<a id="how-do-specified-processing-or-preparation-steps-change-the-measured-metal-endpoints"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-017"></a>
<a id="how-do-derivatives-concentrates-extracts-and-fractions-differ-from-their-parent-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-018"></a>
<a id="do-changes-reflect-removal-redistribution-moisture-or-yield-change-dilution-or-altered-species-or-availability"></a>

Processed or prepared forms were compared only with unprocessed rice noodles in the same study and group. Rice noodles, peel or outer layer (Pasta) had total arsenic higher at 240 µg/kg, against 160 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (rice noodles, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling">Analytical Results from Inorganic Arsenic in Rice and Rice Products Sampling, September 2013</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">U.S. Food and Drug Administration</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

Forms differ in water content, so a per-kilogram difference is not by itself a measured removal or gain of metal.



<a id="mitigation-options"></a>
## Mitigation for rice noodles

<a id="hmi-ing-019"></a>
<a id="which-prevention-mitigation-or-remediation-measures-have-been-evaluated-for-this-ingredient"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-020"></a>
<a id="under-what-conditions-at-which-stage-and-against-which-comparator-do-they-work-or-fail"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-021"></a>
<a id="what-evidence-supports-field-or-commercial-implementation-and-ongoing-verification"></a>

Lot testing against the applicable limit is the check that can be verified.

<p class="hmi-mitigation-gap" data-mitigation-gap>No measured way to lower metals in this food is in the library yet.</p>



<a id="trade-offs-and-failure-modes"></a>
## Trade-offs and limits of controls

<a id="hmi-ing-022"></a>
<a id="can-an-intervention-increase-another-contaminant-or-redistribute-contamination-to-a-by-product"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-023"></a>
<a id="what-effects-on-nutrition-yield-sensory-quality-stability-and-waste-streams-were-measured"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-024"></a>
<a id="what-costs-constraints-adverse-effects-or-failure-modes-are-documented-and-which-are-unknown"></a>

Metals do not move together, so a lot that passes a lead limit says little about cadmium, arsenic or nickel unless those are tested as well.



<a id="sampling-and-testing"></a>
## Testing rice noodles for metals

<a id="what-sampling-design-is-appropriate-for-the-ingredient-heterogeneity-lot-and-decision"></a>
<a id="hmi-ing-026"></a>

Results depend on the method and its reporting limit. Reporting limits for lead ranged from 1 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food) to 120 µg/kg (WHO GEMS/Food), so a non-detect from a less sensitive method says much less.<sup <a id="procurement-and-process-control"></a>
## Buying and verifying rice noodles

No maximum level for metals in rice noodles was verified from primary text for this page; buyers should confirm the limit that applies in the destination market.



<a id="finished-product-and-exposure-implications"></a>
## Exposure from rice noodles

<a id="hmi-ing-031"></a>

No source in the library converted rice noodles concentrations into a verified estimate of intake for a defined population. Concentrations describe the food, not individual risk.

<a id="universal-faqs"></a>
## Rice noodles FAQs

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-rice-noodles" data-anchor="what-heavy-metals-are-found-in-rice-noodles" data-question="What heavy metals are found in rice noodles?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What heavy metals are found in rice noodles?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The library reports lead, cadmium, total arsenic, inorganic arsenic, dimethylarsinic acid, monomethylarsonic acid, total mercury, methylmercury, nickel, chromium, aluminium, tin, antimony, uranium, V, Se, AsIII and AsV in rice noodles, most often lead, cadmium and total arsenic.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/guo2017-asian-rice-derived-products-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Guo K, Wells S, Han FX, Arslan Z, Sun H, Zhang J · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/guo2017-asian-rice-derived-products-metals">Trace Elements and Heavy Metals in Asian Rice-Derived Food Products</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Water, Air, &amp; Soil Pollution</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/guo2017-asian-rice-derived-products-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety (Hong Kong) · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Metallic Contaminants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> WHO GEMS/Food submissions reported lead in rice noodles, as sold from 41 results in 3 reporting regions, with subgroup medians from 3 to 7.85 µg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-rice-noodles" data-anchor="which-regions-report-the-lowest-levels-in-rice-noodles" data-question="Which regions report the lowest levels in rice noodles?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which regions report the lowest levels in rice noodles?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Among GEMS/Food reporting regions, rice noodles, as sold had the lowest lead subgroup median in WPRO (3 µg/kg) and the highest in PAHO (7.85 µg/kg); reporting regions are markets, not growing areas.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For cadmium, the lowest regional median was in EURO (15 µg/kg) and the highest in WPRO (21.5 µg/kg).<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-rice-noodles" data-anchor="does-processing-change-heavy-metals-in-rice-noodles" data-question="Does processing change heavy metals in rice noodles?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does processing change heavy metals in rice noodles?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only comparisons between forms in the same study are available, not before-and-after measurements of the same rice noodles.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling">Analytical Results from Inorganic Arsenic in Rice and Rice Products Sampling, September 2013</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">U.S. Food and Drug Administration</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Rice noodles, peel or outer layer (Pasta) had total arsenic higher at 240 µg/kg, against 160 µg/kg for the unprocessed form in the same group (rice noodles, as sold).<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling">Analytical Results from Inorganic Arsenic in Rice and Rice Products Sampling, September 2013</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">U.S. Food and Drug Administration</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2013-ias-rice-products-sampling">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-rice-noodles-is-inorganic" data-anchor="how-much-of-the-arsenic-in-rice-noodles-is-inorganic" data-question="How much of the arsenic in rice noodles is inorganic?">
